Subject: Security & Compliance - SOC 2 status and roadmap (FinCo) - Post-call recap

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for your time on the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

- SOC 2: you mentioned FinCo has a SOC 2 Type II in progress with an auditor and expect report availability in Q4 2027. Please confirm whether the current scope includes data processing for third-party vendors.
- GDPR / HIPAA: you indicated some EU users and a subset of PHI workloads; we should confirm whether HIPAA obligations will apply to the Redwood-hosted components or only to FinCo's ingestion layer.
- Vendor questionnaire: please share the completed vendor security questionnaire (attached) and any supporting evidence (policies, diagrams).
- Roadmap ask: you expressed interest in ISO 27001 and FedRAMP readiness in the roadmap — we captured this as a potential multi-quarter engagement.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Please return the vendor questionnaire we sent (attached) with any supporting docs by EOD Wednesday (2027-04-28).
2) I'll loop in our security lead (Rishi) to answer technical questions and confirm SOC scoping.
3) Follow-up call (30 min) week of May 3 — propose Tue May 4 or Wed May 5 (I will send a poll).

Attachments: FinCo_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (blank template included on the call).

Let me know if anything above needs correction. Looking forward to progressing this — appreciate the clarity you provided today.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — this looks right. A few clarifications: 

- SOC 2: Correct — we're currently engaged with NorthBridge Audit for a Type II and the scope includes SaaS vendor integrations that process customer data. Expected completion is internal target of 2027-11-15 (auditor deliverable may trail).
- HIPAA: We have a small set of customers where PHI flows through our ingestion endpoint. We'll need Redwood to sign a DPA + BAA if we determine you will process PHI in production.
- ISO/FedRAMP: We're exploring ISO 27001 next year and will evaluate FedRAMP only if we move into government verticals.

Attached: FinCo_Vendor_Questionnaire_Answers.pdf (partial answers filled; see sections 2, 4, and 6). I'll complete the remaining sections by Wednesday.

Also looping in Tom Rivera (tom.rivera@finco.com) — he runs security operations and may have additional evidence requests.

Cheers,
Alice
Senior Procurement Manager, FinCo

Alice / Tom —

Thanks for the partial questionnaire — appreciate the quick turn. Looping in Rishi (security lead) to answer the technical sections and confirm our current artifacts. Rishi, quick context: FinCo processes a subset of PHI and is asking about DPA/BAA, SOC 2 scope, and longer-term interest in ISO 27001 / FedRAMP readiness. They expect the SOC 2 Type II deliverable around mid-November.

Rishi, could you: 
- Confirm which of our hosted components currently fall under SOC 2 scope and whether we can provide interim evidence (policies, SOC-type controls mapping)?
- Confirm our standard DPA/BAA stance and lead time for review.
- Suggest initial evidence list FinCo should expect (e.g., network diagrams, encryption-at-rest docs, access control matrix, recent penetration test summary).

Also: Alice, I added a shared folder with our compliance pack here: https://redwood.app/drive/FinCo-compliance-pack — feel free to drop any evidence there.

Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@finco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Security & Compliance - SOC 2 status and roadmap (FinCo) - Post-call recap

Hi Alice / Marissa —

Thanks for the context — quick answers and next steps below. 

1) Current SOC 2 scope: our hosted API, model inference runtime, and control plane are covered under our SOC 2 Type II (internal scope). We're in the final stages of our 2026 audit cycle; we can produce interim control descriptions and a partial report (attached: SOC2_partial-report-2026.pdf) for vendor review. Full Type II report will align with our next audit window (Q4 2027).

2) DPA / BAA: Redwood has a standard DPA that includes HIPAA language; we can surface a BAA addendum for PHI. Typical legal review cycle is 2-4 weeks depending on redlines. If expedited, we can prioritize during procurement intake.

3) Evidence checklist (minimum to start vendor review):
   - Network diagram (high level)
   - Data flow diagram for PHI (if applicable)
   - Encryption at rest/in transit summary
   - Access control matrix and recent IAM audit log excerpts
   - Recent pen test summary (last 12 months)

4) ISO / FedRAMP roadmap: ISO 27001 is feasible as a 6-12 month program after SOC baseline and mature policy artefacts. FedRAMP is a separate, multi-year undertaking and typically only pursued for sustained government revenue — we can provide an assessment of gaps if that's a priority.

Attachments: SOC2_partial-report-2026.pdf (redacted), FinCo_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (completed sections and comments).

Next steps: 
- Marissa: please share a 30-min slot for May 4.
- Alice / Tom: please upload the remaining questionnaire answers and any diagrams to the shared Drive link.
- I'll prepare a short evidence pack and control mapping to SOC 2 that we can share during the follow-up.

Regards,

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security | Redwood Inference
